The commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 93, verses 1–3:

Meccan, and its verses number 11. "It was revealed after the dawn."

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

By "al-Duha" (the forenoon) is meant the time of forenoon, which is the early part of the day until the sun rises high and casts its light. It is said that the forenoon was singled out for the oath because it is the hour when Musa (peace be upon him) was addressed and when the sorcerers were cast down in prostration, based on His saying ﴿and that people be gathered in the forenoon﴾. It is also said that "al-Duha" means the day, as clarified by His saying ﴿that Our punishment come upon them in the forenoon﴾, in contrast with "by night" (bayatan).

"Saja" means it became still and its darkness settled. It is said: a still night, with the wind calm. It is also said that it means the stillness of people and sounds in it. And "sajā al-bahr" means the sea's waves became calm.

"Tarf sāj" means a gaze that is still and languid.

﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you﴾ is the answer to the oath. Its meaning is: He has not cut you off in the manner of one who bids farewell.

It has also been read with the lighter form, meaning: He has not left you. The poet said:

"And there we left the family of ʿAmr and ʿĀmir
as prey for the tips of the straight, dark spears."

[[Thumma is a reference to the place or time of the battle. Scholars differed over "daʿa" meaning "to leave," whether it is conjugated so that it has a past tense, a verbal noun, an active participle and a passive participle. Al-Jawhari said: its past tense and other forms are not used, though it may occur in poetry by necessity. This is the well-known view, but where it occurs in the Qur'an it is in the form ﴿mā waddaʿaka﴾ with the lighter spelling. In a hadith: "Let people cease from abandoning the congregational prayers," meaning leaving them.

The passive participle and other forms do occur in poetry, so the view is that the usage is rare, not that the verb is obsolete, as some earlier scholars stated. "Al-Faraʾis" is the second object; it is the plural of farisa, which is the prey of a lion. "Al-Muthaqqafa" means the spears straightened with the thaqaf, which is the instrument used to straighten spears. "Al-Summara" is a color between whiteness and brownness. The spears are compared to black things by way of metaphor (al-makniyya, metaphor by allusion), and "the prey" is imaginative representation (takhyil). The more apt reading is that the family of ʿAmr and the family of ʿĀmir are likened to prey in an eloquent simile, given the mention of the tips, unless one says it is an abstraction (tajrid) of the metaphor, since it suits the spears.]]

"Tawdīʿ" is an intensification of "wadʿ," because one who bids you farewell while departing has gone to the extreme of leaving you.

It is related that revelation was delayed from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for some days. The polytheists said: Muhammad's Lord has bid him farewell and come to hate him. [[Ibn Mardawayh transmitted it from the narration of al-ʿAwfi, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He hated you﴾: "Gabriel was delayed in coming to him," and so on.]]

It was also said: Umm Jamil, the wife of Abu Lahab, said to him: "O Muhammad, I do not think your devil has left you except." So this was revealed. [[Agreed upon, from the hadith of Jundub ibn ʿAbdullah al-Bajali, with the wording: "A woman came and said: O Muhammad, I hope your devil has left you." So God revealed ﴿By the forenoon﴾. In al-Mustadrak, from the hadith of Zayd ibn Arqam: "The Prophet (ﷺ) remained for some days without revelation coming to him. Then the wife of Abu Lahab came to him and said: O Muhammad," and he mentioned something similar.]]

The pronoun is omitted from "qalā" just as it is omitted from "al-dhākirāt" in His saying ﴿the men who remember God much and the women who remember﴾, meaning "and the women who remember Him." Similarly ﴿fa-āwā … fa-hadā … fa-aghnā﴾ (He sheltered you … and guided you … and enriched you). This is verbal abbreviation, since the omitted element is clear.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 93, verse 4–5:

If you ask: how does His saying ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the former life﴾ connect with what precedes it? I answer: since it implies the denial of abandonment and of hatred, namely that God is continuing to bestow revelation upon you [[Mahmud said: "If you ask: how does it connect with what precedes it? He answered that since it implies the denial of abandonment and hatred, that God is continuing to bestow revelation upon you... etc." Ahmad said: and the bringing out of the people of major sins from the Fire through his intercession is added to that.]], and that you are the beloved of God, and you see no honour greater than this nor any blessing more magnificent than it, He informs him that his station in the Hereafter is greater and more magnificent than that. It is precedence and preeminence over all the prophets and messengers of God, the testimony of his community over all other nations, the raising of the ranks of the believers and the elevation of their levels through his intercession, and other sublime honours. ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, so that you will be well pleased﴾: a comprehensive promise encompassing what He gave him in this world of victory and triumph over his enemies on the day of Badr and on the day of the conquest of Makkah, the entry of people into the religion in multitudes, the subjugation of Qurayzah and al-Nadir and their expulsion, the dispatch of his armies and expeditions throughout the lands of Arabia, what was opened to his rightly-guided successors in the regions of the earth, the cities, the destruction by their hands of the kingdoms of the tyrants, the plundering of the treasures of the Chosroes, the terror cast into the hearts of the peoples of East and West and their awe of Islam [[His saying "and their awe of Islam" (tahayyub al-Islam): i.e., fear, as in al-Sihah, that is, the people's fear of the people of Islam. (A)]], the spread of the call and the dominance of the Muslims, and what He has stored up for him of reward whose true nature none knows but God. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: "He has in Paradise a thousand palaces of white pearl whose dust is musk."

If you ask: what is this lam that enters upon "sawfa"? I answer: it is the lam of initiation (lam al-ibtida') emphasizing the content of the sentence, and the subject is omitted. Its estimate: "And you, surely He will give you," as we mentioned in: ﴿I swear not﴾, that the meaning is: "Indeed I swear," since it cannot be other than either the lam of oath or the lam of initiation. The lam of oath does not enter upon the present-tense verb except with the emphatic nun, so it remains that it is the lam of initiation, and the lam of initiation does not enter except upon a nominal sentence consisting of subject and predicate, so an estimated subject and predicate is necessary, and its origin is: "And you, surely He will give you."

If you ask: what is the meaning of combining the two particles of emphasis and deferment? I answer: its meaning is that the giving is certain to occur without doubt, even if it is delayed, because of the benefit contained in the delay.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 93, verses 6–8:

He enumerated for him His blessings and favours, and that He had not left him devoid of them from the first moment of his upbringing and the beginning of his growth, as a preparation for what He intended for him, so that he might measure what was awaited from God's bounty by what had already passed from Him, lest he expect anything but the best and an increase of good and honour:

"And [He did not] constrict his breast or diminish his patience." And ﴿Did He not find you﴾ [alam yajidka], here the verb is from wajada in the sense of "knowing" (al-wujud alladhi bi-ma'na al-'ilm), and the two accusatives are its two objects. The meaning is: Were you not an orphan? For his father died while he was in the womb, six months after conception, and his mother died when he was eight years old, so his uncle Abu Talib took him in charge, and God inclined him towards him, and he raised him well.

Among the strange interpretations is that it derives from the saying "a unique pearl" (durra yatima), and that the meaning is: Did He not find you unique among the Quraysh, without equal, and so give you shelter? It has also been read as ﴿fa-awa﴾, which has two meanings: either it is from awahu, in the sense of "gave him shelter" (a'wahu). Some herdsmen were heard saying: "Where does he shelter this mangy camel?" [Note: "He says 'where does he shelter this mangy camel' — al-Mawqasa: the mangy camel, from al-waqs, which is the onset of mange." According to the Sihah: "waqasahu wagsan" means he afflicted him, and "in al-ba'ir la-waqsan" means a camel has been touched by some mange, so it is mawquus. (Editor's gloss.)] Or it is from awa lahu, meaning he showed him mercy.

﴿Wa-wajadaka dallan﴾ [and He found you astray]: the meaning is straying from knowledge of the sacred law and what is known only through revelation, as in His saying: ﴿You did not know what the Book was﴾. It is also said: he strayed in his childhood in some valleys of Mecca, and Abu Jahl returned him to Abd al-Muttalib. It is also said: Halima lost him near the gate of Mecca when she weaned him and brought him back to return him to Abd al-Muttalib. It is also said: he strayed on the road to Syria when Abu Talib took him out, ﴿and guided you﴾: He made the Qur'an and the laws known to you. Or: He removed your straying from your grandfather and your uncle.

As for one who says he was upon the religion of his people for forty years: if he means that he was free of their scholarly ignorance, then yes; but if he means that he followed their religion and their disbelief, then God forbid. Prophets must be protected from grave sins and from shameful minor sins both before and after prophethood. So what of disbelief and ignorance of the Creator? ﴿It was not for us to associate anything with God﴾. And it is enough of a defect in the eyes of the disbelievers that a prophet should previously have been in disbelief.

﴿And He found you poor [ta'ilan]﴾: a poor man. It has also been read ʿaylan, as ﴿sayyiḥat﴾ is read. ﴿Wa-wajadaka 'adiman [and He found you in need]﴾ [or destitute], ﴿fa-aghna﴾: so He enriched you with the wealth of Khadija, or with the spoils He bestowed upon you. He (ﷺ) said: "My provision has been placed under the shade of my spear." [This is a fragment of a hadith. It was narrated by al-Bukhari in suspended form, and by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Ibn Abi Shayba, and Abd ibn Humayd; and by Abu Ya'la, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, from Abdullah ibn Umar. In al-Nasa'i it is narrated from Abu Hurayra; al-Bazzar narrated it from the report of Sadaqa ibn Abdullah from al-Awza'i from Yahya from Abu Salama from Abu Hurayra, and he said: no one followed Sadaqa in this. Others narrate it from al-Awza'i as a mursal report. It has another chain in the biography of Ahmad ibn Mahmud in the Tarikh Isfahan of Abu Nu'aym, with its chain going back to Anas. Its chain is weak.]

It has also been said: "He made you content and enriched your heart."

﴿Wa-wajadaka dallan﴾ [and He found you astray]: the meaning is straying from knowledge of the sacred law and what is known only through revelation, as in His saying: ﴿You did not know what the Book was﴾. It is also said: he strayed in his childhood in some valleys of Mecca, and Abu Jahl returned him to Abd al-Muttalib. It is also said: Halima lost him near the gate of Mecca when she weaned him and brought him back to return him to Abd al-Muttalib. It is also said: he strayed on the road to Syria when Abu Talib took him out, ﴿and guided you﴾: He made the Qur'an and the laws known to you. Or: He removed your straying from your grandfather and your uncle.

As for one who says he was upon the religion of his people for forty years: if he means that he was free of their scholarly ignorance, then yes; but if he means that he followed their religion and their disbelief, then God forbid. Prophets must be protected from grave sins and from shameful minor sins both before and after prophethood. So what of disbelief and ignorance of the Creator? ﴿It was not for us to associate anything with God﴾. And it is enough of a defect in the eyes of the disbelievers that a prophet should previously have been in disbelief.

﴿And He found you poor [ta'ilan]﴾: a poor man. It has also been read ʿaylan, as ﴿sayyiḥat﴾ is read. ﴿Wa-wajadaka 'adiman [and He found you in need]﴾ [or destitute], ﴿fa-aghna﴾: so He enriched you with the wealth of Khadija, or with the spoils He bestowed upon you. He (ﷺ) said: "My provision has been placed under the shade of my spear." [This is a fragment of a hadith. It was narrated by al-Bukhari in suspended form, and by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Ibn Abi Shayba, and Abd ibn Humayd; and by Abu Ya'la, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, from Abdullah ibn Umar. In al-Nasa'i it is narrated from Abu Hurayra; al-Bazzar narrated it from the report of Sadaqa ibn Abdullah from al-Awza'i from Yahya from Abu Salama from Abu Hurayra, and he said: no one followed Sadaqa in this. Others narrate it from al-Awza'i as a mursal report. It has another chain in the biography of Ahmad ibn Mahmud in the Tarikh Isfahan of Abu Nu'aym, with its chain going back to Anas. Its chain is weak.]

It has also been said: "He made you content and enriched your heart."
